did_you_know.text: The chapter opens with Elkanah’s genealogy: he was the son of Jeroham, the son of Elihu, the son of Tohu, the son of Zuph. He is described as an Ephraimite from Ramathaim-zophim in the hill country of Ephraim.
Every year, Elkanah went up to Shiloh to worship the LORD and offer sacrifices to him. At that time, Eli’s sons Hophni and Phinehas were serving there as priests of the LORD.
Elkanah loved Hannah and gave her a special portion, even though the LORD had closed her womb and she had no children.
Elkanah tried to comfort Hannah and asked her whether his love for her was not better than having ten sons.
In her prayer, Hannah vowed that if she were given a son, she would dedicate him to the LORD for all the days of his life, and no razor would ever touch his head.
Hannah was praying silently: her lips moved, but her voice could not be heard. Eli the priest saw her and mistakenly thought she was drunk.
After Hannah explained to Eli that she was pouring out her soul before the LORD, Eli blessed her and said that the LORD would grant her request.
After her prayer, Hannah became pregnant and gave birth to a son. She named him Samuel, saying that she had asked the LORD for him.
Hannah did not go up to Shiloh immediately after Samuel was born. Instead, she waited until he was weaned, so that she could bring him to the house of the LORD and leave him there.

Hannah explained to Eli that Samuel was the child for whom she had prayed, and she dedicated him to the LORD for all his days. Thus, the chapter ends with Samuel being entrusted to the LORD’s service at Shiloh.
